metadata.title: Matthew Hibner - Two catches in Week 4 win
metadata.description: Hibner caught both of his targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 24-18 win over the Titans.
metadata.analysis: Both Hibner and Mark Andrews played 37 of 64 offensive snaps against Tennessee, though Andrews ran 24 routes to Hibner's 10, as the latter is more of the blocking complement to Andrews in the pass-catching role. The fourth-round rookie Hibner has secured all five of his targets for 70 yards and a touchdown through four games.

metadata.title: Matt Hibner finds the end zone in Week 3
metadata.description: Matt Hibner caught both of his targets for 23 yards and a touchdown in a 34-31 win over the Cowboys in Week 3.
metadata.analysis: Hibner found the end zone on a two-yard pass from Lamar Jackson to put the Ravens up 30-28 in the fourth quarter. The rookie tight end has caught three passes for 36 yards and one touchdown through three games. He will now get ready to face the Titans in Week 4.

metadata.title: Matthew Hibner - Catches sole target in win
metadata.description: Hibner caught his only target for 13 yards in the Ravens' 41-23 win over the Colts on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Hibner played 23 offensive snaps in the contest, shifting into the offense when the Ravens lined up for 13-personnel packages. The fourth-round rookie also played nine special teams snaps, displaying his versatility as a 6-foot-4, 251-pound tight end.

metadata.title: Matt Hibner catches one pass in Week 1
metadata.description: Matt Hibner caught his only target for 13 yards in the Ravens' 41-23 win over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 1.
metadata.analysis: Hibner joined Durham Smythe in finishing behind veteran Mark Andrews in tight end targets in the win. The rookie can be left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 2 contest against the New Orleans Saints.

metadata.title: Matthew Hibner - Two catches to close preseason
metadata.description: Hibner caught two of three targets for 11 yards in Friday's 41-3 preseason win over the Commanders.
metadata.analysis: Eight different Ravens caught multiple passes in the rout as neither team used their starters, and Hibner worked with the first-team offense, catching one pass from Tyler Huntley and another from Joe Fagnano. Hibner, a fourth-round rookie out of SMU, is fighting for snaps and targets at tight end behind veterans Mark Andrews and Durham Smythe, with his main competition being fellow first-year player Josh Cuevas.

metadata.title: Matthew Hibner - Blanked vs. Minnesota
metadata.description: Hibner failed to haul in his two targets during the Ravens' 13-3 preseason win over the Vikings on Saturday.
metadata.analysis: Both Hibner and Josh Cuevas were listed as the Ravens' starting tight ends Saturday while Mark Andrews and Durham Smythe did not play. Hibner couldn't haul in either target form Joe Faganano in the second half, though the Ravens offense as a whole struggled to just 193 passing yards. Hibner, a fourth-round rookie out of SMU, is competing against Smythe for the TE2 role behind Andrews, though Hibner will likely start the regular season as the third-string tight end. The Ravens' preseason finale takes place Friday against the Commanders.

metadata.title: Matt Hibner Turns Heads in Preseason Opener
metadata.description: Baltimore Ravens rookie tight end Matt Hibner hauled in all five of his targets for 61 yards in the Ravens' 24-7 preseason victory over the Philadelphia Eagles. Hibner ran a variety of routes and demonstrated robust rapport with veteran quarterback Tyler Huntley and rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano alike, indicating Hibner's hard work during camp is making its way onto the field. Notably, Hibner caught a 29-yard pass from Huntley on the Ravens' second offensive play, setting the tone for first-time play caller Declan Doyle's new offense. The Ravens traded up during the draft to grab the SMU tight end in the fourth round even after extending veteran tight end Mark Andrews at the tail end of the 2025 season and signing blocking tight end Durham Smythe in March. Dynasty managers, particularly those in tight end premium leagues, should keep Hibner on their radar with eyes towards the latter half of the season when rookie production tends to surge.

metadata.title: Matthew Hibner - Impresses in preseason opener
metadata.description: Hibner brought in all five targets for 61 yards in the Ravens' 24-7 preseason win over the Eagles on Saturday.
metadata.analysis: The rookie fourth-round pick wasted no time making an impact, recording a 29-yard reception on the Ravens' second play from scrimmage. Hibner added gains of eight and 13 yards on his next two catches, and the SMU product ultimately played into the second half. Hibner finished second on the night in all of receptions, receiving yards and targets for Baltimore, and it may not be long before he makes a case to usurp journeyman Durham Smythe for the No. 2 tight end job.

metadata.title: Is Matthew Hibner the Tight End of the Future in Baltimore?
metadata.description: The Baltimore Ravens made an aggressive move in the fourth round of the 2026 Draft, trading up to acquire SMU tight end Matthew Hibner. Across 13 games as a fifth-year senior in 2025, Hibner hauled in 31 receptions for 436 yards and four touchdowns. The Ravens have veteran tight end Mark Andrews firmly atop their depth chart, and they also signed tight end Durham Smythe in free agency. However, Baltimore lost key depth at the position over the offseason, with Isaiah Likely and Charlie Kolar both departing the team in free agency. Along with Ravens' fifth-round selection Josh Cuevas, Hibner should have a chance to play a prominent role alongside Andrews as a rookie. Andrews is also entering his age-31 season in 2026, so Hibner could emerge as Baltimore's tight end of the future with a solid rookie campaign. In dynasty leagues, Hibner is a name for managers to monitor.

metadata.title: Matthew Hibner signs rookie deal with Ravens
metadata.description: The Ravens signed fourth-round TE Matthew Hibner to a four-year contract.
metadata.analysis: Hibner's deal is worth $5 million. He'll be competing for a depth spot in the Ravens tight end room.

metadata.title: Matthew Hibner - Added by Ravens
metadata.description: The Ravens selected Hibner in the fourth round of the 2026 NFL Draft, 133rd overall.
metadata.analysis: The Ravens lost tight ends Isaiah Likely to the Giants and Charlie Kolar to the Chargers in free agency, so they're likely hoping Hibner along with free-agent addition Durham Smythe can add immediate depth behind Mark Andrews. Hibner spent six years in college. He caught just two passes through his first four seasons at Michigan before transferring to SMU for his final two years of eligibility and producing 55 receptions for 804 yards and eight touchdowns over 27 games. Hibner is an impressive athlete with a 4.57 40-yard dash at 6-foot-4, 251 pounds, and he's a strong route runner with dependable hands. However, he'll need to immediately prove that his blocking skills can translate to the NFL before he establishes himself in the rotation.

metadata.title: Matthew Hibner selected No. 133 by Baltimore Ravens
metadata.description: The Baltimore Ravens have selected TE Matthew Hibner with the No. 133 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
metadata.analysis: Baltimore traded up to draft Hibner out of SMU. He'll add to the Ravens tight end room after losing Isaiah Likely in free agency. He tested well at the combine and is a natural route runner. He'll compete for an immediate role behind Mark Andrews.
